name: Grumman G-44 Widgeon
summary: Small amphibious flying boat built from 1941 to the late 1940s, with two engines on a high wing; many fly in Alaska, the Caribbean and Pacific Northwest.

wings: Small stabilizing floats near the wingtips
engines: Two engines on the wing leading edge, close to the hull
Engine type varies by version: inline, radial or flat-six
fuselage: Short, deep boat hull with a stepped bottom
Main wheels fold up into the hull sides
Small cockpit windscreen at the front of the hull

tellTales: Short, stubby boat hull with two engines on a high wing
Main wheels that retract into the sides of the hull
Strut-braced horizontal tail on a small amphibian

confusedWith.howToTell: The Goose is much bigger, with large round radial engines and a longer, deeper hull with more windows; the Widgeon is a small five-seater.
The Mallard is larger, with tricycle gear (nose wheel), wingtip tanks and a long row of square windows.
The HU-16 Albatross is far larger, with two big radials, a tall tail and a long hull with Navy or Coast Guard markings.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
